problems.title: Polewise supremum normalization destroys Green-kernel symmetry
problems.source_locator: Page 6 Green equation and normalization; page 8 proof of Proposition 3.3 before (3.6), (3.7)
problems.all_hypotheses: Compact klt Kahler space, bounded canonical MA metric and smooth resolution approximants; Property (P); nonnegative C2 function with f and negative Laplacian in sufficiently high Lp. Counterexample: smooth CP1 with g_eta=(1+eta(3z^2-1)/2)g0, 0<eta<1, area 4pi; canonical density equals omega_eta and cutoffs are constant.
problems.decisive_evidence: The exact symmetric mean-zero kernel is K_eta=G0+eta(Yx+Yy)/(24pi)-eta^2/(120pi). Antipodal maxima for pole and equatorial points are proved analytically; m(P)-m(E)=eta/(8pi). Thus sup-normalized G_P(E)-G_E(P)=-eta/(8pi).
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json, P01_Green_symmetry. At eta=0.5 the discrepancy is -0.01989436788648692. Sampling corroborates the analytic maximum inequality.
problems.counterevidence: The mean-zero kernel is symmetric. GPSS v1 equation (5.17), page 19, uses a global shift over both variables. Self-adjointness does not rescue a pole-dependent shift.
problems.core_dependency: Proposition 3.3 -> Corollary 5.11 -> Theorem 5.15 -> current closure Theorem 5.17 -> BG proof.
problems.repair: Uniform L1 and a positive volume lower bound imply a uniform bound for m_epsilon. Set Gtilde=K-M with M>=sup(m+1). The Lp estimate survives a bounded shift, the second-variable gradient is unchanged, and the weighted gradient bound improves. A common off-diagonal subsequence preserves symmetry.
problems.impact_boundary: Invalid identity in a central derivation, even though its normalization repair is local. Neither Proposition 3.3 nor the final BG theorem is shown false.

independent_verification.claim_and_assumptions: Independently read source pp.4,6-8 and confirmed Property(P), polewise sup=-1 normalization, and the explicit appeal to symmetry before (3.6)/(3.7). Smooth CP1 is within the general-dimensional Proposition3.3, with positive density 1+eta*P2 for 0<eta<1 and constant cutoffs.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Recomputed the Poisson identity using Delta0 P2=-6P2 and conformal scaling, the zero-mean constant from integral P2^2=4pi/5, and the antipodal maximum bound log((1-t)/2)<=-(1+t)/2 with z^2<=2(1+t). The pole/equator maxima differ eta/(8pi), so the displayed sup-normalized kernel cannot be symmetric.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: The symmetric mean-zero kernel does not have the prescribed polewise maximum. A single M>=sup(m_epsilon+1) exists by the uniform L1 bound and volume lower bound; K-M preserves symmetry, the bounded-shift Lp estimate and the improved weighted gradient bound. Independently read GPSS v1 p.19 eq.(5.17), which uses a global infimum.
independent_verification.impact_and_grade: Source p.20 explicitly transfers the proof of Proposition3.3 to Corollary5.11; pp.24-25 and29-30 establish its dependence chain into the main theorem. Major concerns an invalid core derivation; neither the boundedness conclusion nor BG is refuted.

problems.title: The gradient-norm potential is not smooth orbifold metric and depends on embedding
problems.source_locator: Orbifold definition page 9; Theorem 4.3 pages 11-12; Claim 4.4 and (4.5) page 12; three embedding assertions and gluing page 13
problems.all_hypotheses: Compact normal klt Kahler threefold; Z is the nonorbifold locus; remaining singularities are A1 surface double points along a smooth curve. X=P(1,1,2) times P1 satisfies these assumptions with Z empty. The local uniformization is (u,v,z) -> (u^2,v^2,uv,z).
problems.decisive_evidence: F_c=sqrt(|u|^4+|v|^4+c|u|^2|v|^2) has Levi_uu(r,0)=1 and Levi_uu(0,r)=c/2. Claim 4.4 uses c=1 and the actual gradient formula c=4; neither extends continuously at zero. Adding the redundant equation w gives sqrt(1+F4^2), whose potential ratio is unbounded and whose Levi_uu(r,0)=(2r^2+r^6)/(1+r^4)^(3/2) tends to zero instead of one.
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json, P02_Levi_and_embedding and P02_redundant_embedding. Exact rational axis values and ordinary floating-point corroboration.
problems.counterevidence: Euclidean comparability remains valid. The local potential sqrt(|Z1|^2+|Z2|^2+2|Z3|^2) pulls back to |u|^2+|v|^2. The example is A1 and within the assumptions.
problems.core_dependency: The explicit construction is the proof of substantive secondary Theorem 4.3.
problems.repair: Use potentials with genuinely smooth orbifold pullbacks; justify compatible gluing and resolution Lp determinant bounds near Z.
problems.impact_boundary: No false metric existence theorem established. Main Section 5 uses a different interpolating metric, based on a genuine orbifold metric outside a neighborhood of finitely many points.

independent_verification.claim_and_assumptions: Read the orbifold smoothness definition on p.9, full Theorem4.3 assumptions on pp.11-12 and unrestricted embedding/gluing on p.13. P(1,1,2) times P1 has only A1 surface quotients times a smooth curve and empty non-orbifold locus.
independent_verification.decisive_check: For F(s,t)=sqrt(s^2+t^2+cst), Levi_uu=F_s+s*F_ss gives 1 on the u-axis and c/2 on the v-axis. Source Claim4.4 uses c=1 and its gradient norm uses c=4, both incompatible with continuous Hessian extension. For sqrt(1+s^2) on the u-axis, Levi_uu=s/sqrt(1+s^2)+s/(1+s^2)^(3/2)=(2r^2+r^6)/(1+r^4)^(3/2), which tends to zero; adding an ambient pullback contributes O(r^2).
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: Euclidean comparability away from zero does not imply smooth orbifold extension. The c=2 potential is a genuine local smooth repair, but it does not by itself supply gluing or global Lp control. A redundant equation w is permitted by the source arbitrary-embedding formulation.
independent_verification.impact_and_grade: Major applies to the explicit construction that constitutes Theorem4.3. Source pp.16-17 independently construct the main-proof interpolation from a genuine orbifold metric; the report correctly avoids transferring this particular defect wholesale to BG.

problems.title: Incorrect mass normalization in the regularized Monge-Ampere equation
problems.source_locator: Equation (2.3), page 5, and c_epsilon=V_epsilon/V, page 6; contrast the normalizing constant on page 19
problems.all_hypotheses: Log resolution of a compact klt Kahler space, SNC exceptional divisors with discrepancies ai>-1, smooth divisor norms, fixed smooth positive volume form with unsmoothed mass V. Example X=P(1,1,1,2), exceptional P2 of normal bundle O(-2), discrepancy 1/2 by adjunction.
problems.decisive_evidence: I_epsilon=integral sqrt(|s|^2+epsilon^2)dVhat is strictly greater than V. The printed right-hand side has mass V_epsilon I_epsilon/V>V_epsilon, while the left-hand side has cohomological mass V_epsilon.
problems.independent_computation: checks/independent_checks_001.json, P03_mass_normalization. The global mass inequality is proved analytically and is not represented as a numerical integration.
problems.counterevidence: The scalar V_epsilon/I_epsilon restores mass equality. The klt SNC assumptions give dominated convergence I_epsilon -> V, so the coefficient tends to one and the uniform Lp and smooth-away estimates persist.
problems.core_dependency: Construction of smooth canonical MA approximants before the Green estimates.
problems.impact_boundary: An isolated scalar correction. It does not refute canonical MA existence or the final BG theorem.

independent_verification.claim_and_assumptions: Independently read the fixed smooth volume form and unsmoothed mass V on p.5, c_epsilon=V_epsilon/V on p.6, and the separate correctly normalizing constant on p.19.
independent_verification.decisive_check: Adjunction on E=P2 with normal O(-2) gives K_Xhat|E=O(-1), hence discrepancy a=1/2 for P(1,1,1,2). For epsilon>0, sqrt(|s|^2+epsilon^2)>|s| pointwise, so the printed RHS mass is strictly greater than the cohomological LHS mass.
independent_verification.counterevidence_and_repair: c_epsilon=V_epsilon/I_epsilon restores the exact compatibility condition. For SNC discrepancies a_i>-1, choose p>1 with p*a_i>-1 for negative a_i; dominated convergence yields I_epsilon to V and preserves the Lp bound.
independent_verification.impact_and_grade: Minor is retained for this local displayed normalization: the main interpolation uses its own properly normalized equation on p.19. No distinct central dependency on the wrong scalar was established. This grading does not rely on repair ease or require whole-paper failure.
